What a plot sends to MiRA

Source: R/mira.R
mira_spec.Rd

Shows the settings a plot sends to MiRA: those of its components, after merging. Useful to check a plot before opening it.

Usage

mira_spec(x, json = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A mira_plot.

json

FALSE (default) for an R list, TRUE for the JSON string MiRA receives.

Value

A list, or a JSON string.

Details

The list has one element per part of the plot that was set (layout, node, intralayer, interlayer, layer, filter, camera, legend, mode), each with the arguments given, and version, the version of the format. Some settings are shown as MiRA receives them, not as they were written:

  • colors as "#rrggbb";

  • a mira_filter() condition as the names it keeps (node names, layer names, links as layer and node names);

  • color_values, color_scale, color_palette, color_reverse and color_limits under scales, one entry per attribute name, merged over the components (mira_scales); one color per layer under layer$colors.

The network itself is not included. A plot with no components sends only version: MiRA's default view.

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

mira_spec(p + mira_node(color = "red"))
#> $version
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $node
#> $node$color
#> [1] "#ff0000"
#> 
#> 
mira_spec(p + mira_node(color = "red"), json = TRUE)
#> [1] "{\n  \"version\": 1,\n  \"node\": {\n    \"color\": \"#ff0000\"\n  }\n}"
